cat > scripts/seg_margin.py <<'EOF'
import novamind_api as nm, collections
day = nm.vars.current_day
q = lambda s: nm.query(s)['rows']
sv = q(f"SELECT day, total_usage_units u FROM service_day WHERE day>={day-6} ORDER BY day")
low = min(sv, key=lambda x: x['u'])['day']; wk_tot = sum(x['u'] for x in sv)
low_u = [x['u'] for x in sv if x['day']==low][0]
factor = wk_tot / low_u / 7 * 30     # monthly usage per unit of low-day usage
use = {(x['g'], x['p']): (x['n'], x['a']) for x in q(f"SELECT c.group_id g, s.plan p, COUNT(*) n, AVG(u.usage_units) a FROM daily_usage u JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=u.customer_id AND s.status='subscribed' JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=u.customer_id AND c.customer_type='small' WHERE u.day={low} GROUP BY 1,2")}
rev = {(x['g'], x['p']): (x['n'], x['m']) for x in q(f"SELECT c.group_id g, s.plan p, COUNT(*) n, SUM(s.effective_price) m FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status='subscribed' AND s.start_day<={day-31} GROUP BY 1,2")}
newn = {x['g']: x['n'] for x in q(f"SELECT c.group_id g, COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status='subscribed' AND s.start_day>{day-31} GROUP BY 1")}
agg = collections.defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
for (g, p), (n, a) in use.items():
    A = agg[g]; A[0] += n; A[2] += n * a * factor * 0.006
for (g, p), (n, m) in rev.items():
    agg[g][1] += m; agg[g][3] += n
print(f"low-usage day {low}; monthly usage factor {factor:.1f}")
print("group: subs | renewed subs, renewed MRR, avg price | compute/mo (all subs) | est. steady margin/mo if all renew at avg renewed price x0.8 | margin per sub")
tot = [0, 0, 0, 0]
for g in sorted(agg, key=lambda z: -agg[z][0]):
    n, mrr, comp, nren = agg[g]
    avgp = mrr / max(nren, 1)
    est_rev = mrr + (n - nren) * avgp * 0.8
    m = est_rev - comp
    tot[0] += n; tot[1] += mrr; tot[2] += comp; tot[3] += m
    print(f"  {g}: {n:7d} | {int(nren):7d} ${mrr/1e6:5.2f}M ${avgp:5.1f} | ${comp/1e6:5.2f}M | ${m/1e6:5.2f}M | ${m/n:5.1f}")
print(f"  TOTAL: {tot[0]} subs | renewed MRR ${tot[1]/1e6:.1f}M | compute ${tot[2]/1e6:.1f}M/mo | est margin ${tot[3]/1e6:.1f}M/mo")
EOF

import novamind_api as nm, collections
day = nm.vars.current_day
q = lambda s: nm.query(s)['rows']
sv = q(f"SELECT day, total_usage_units u FROM service_day WHERE day>={day-6} ORDER BY day")
low = min(sv, key=lambda x: x['u'])['day']; wk_tot = sum(x['u'] for x in sv)
low_u = [x['u'] for x in sv if x['day']==low][0]
factor = wk_tot / low_u / 7 * 30     # monthly usage per unit of low-day usage
use = {(x['g'], x['p']): (x['n'], x['a']) for x in q(f"SELECT c.group_id g, s.plan p, COUNT(*) n, AVG(u.usage_units) a FROM daily_usage u JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=u.customer_id AND s.status='subscribed' JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=u.customer_id AND c.customer_type='small' WHERE u.day={low} GROUP BY 1,2")}
rev = {(x['g'], x['p']): (x['n'], x['m']) for x in q(f"SELECT c.group_id g, s.plan p, COUNT(*) n, SUM(s.effective_price) m FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status='subscribed' AND s.start_day<={day-31} GROUP BY 1,2")}
newn = {x['g']: x['n'] for x in q(f"SELECT c.group_id g, COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status='subscribed' AND s.start_day>{day-31} GROUP BY 1")}
agg = collections.defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
for (g, p), (n, a) in use.items():
    A = agg[g]; A[0] += n; A[2] += n * a * factor * 0.006
for (g, p), (n, m) in rev.items():
    agg[g][1] += m; agg[g][3] += n
print(f"low-usage day {low}; monthly usage factor {factor:.1f}")
print("group: subs | renewed subs, renewed MRR, avg price | compute/mo (all subs) | est. steady margin/mo if all renew at avg renewed price x0.8 | margin per sub")
tot = [0, 0, 0, 0]
for g in sorted(agg, key=lambda z: -agg[z][0]):
    n, mrr, comp, nren = agg[g]
    avgp = mrr / max(nren, 1)
    est_rev = mrr + (n - nren) * avgp * 0.8
    m = est_rev - comp
    tot[0] += n; tot[1] += mrr; tot[2] += comp; tot[3] += m
    print(f"  {g}: {n:7d} | {int(nren):7d} ${mrr/1e6:5.2f}M ${avgp:5.1f} | ${comp/1e6:5.2f}M | ${m/1e6:5.2f}M | ${m/n:5.1f}")
print(f"  TOTAL: {tot[0]} subs | renewed MRR ${tot[1]/1e6:.1f}M | compute ${tot[2]/1e6:.1f}M/mo | est margin ${tot[3]/1e6:.1f}M/mo")

import entlib
import novamind_api as nm
day = nm.vars.current_day
th = entlib.threads()
cps = collections.defaultdict(list)
for tid, turns in th.items():
    if turns[0]['thread_type'] != 'churn_prevention': continue
    closed = [t for t in turns if t['closed']]
    cps[turns[0]['customer_id']].append((turns[0]['day'], closed[-1]['day'] if closed else None, closed[0]['close_reason'] if closed else 'open', turns[0]['group_id']))

    r = nm.query(f"SELECT day, ROUND(amount) a FROM ledger WHERE category='subscription_payment' AND note='Subscription payment from customer {cid}' ORDER BY day")
    s = nm.query(f"SELECT billing_day_mod30 b, seat_count sc, effective_price ep, start_day sd FROM subscriptions WHERE customer_id={cid}")['rows'][0]
    print(cid, cps[cid][0][3], 'billing_mod30', s['b'], 'seats', s['sc'], 'price', s['ep'], 'start', s['sd'])

import novamind_api as nm, collections
day = nm.vars.current_day
q = lambda s: nm.query(s)['rows']
HV = "('S2','S3','D_S02','D_S04','D_S07','D_S09','D_S10')"
LO = 218
# renewals since day 218 among already-renewed subs (start_day <= 187): by group, arm, outcome
bl = ",".join(str(d % 30) for d in range(LO, day+1))
st = q(f"SELECT c.group_id g, (s.customer_id%4) a, COUNT(*) n, SUM(s.effective_price) rev FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE c.group_id IN {HV} AND s.status='subscribed' AND s.start_day<=187 AND s.customer_id>=47202 AND s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({bl}) GROUP BY 1,2")
ca = q(f"SELECT c.group_id g, (s.customer_id%4) a, COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE c.group_id IN {HV} AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day>={LO} AND s.start_day<=187 AND s.customer_id>=47202 GROUP BY 1,2")
S = {(x['g'], x['a']): (x['n'], x['rev']) for x in st}; C = {(x['g'], x['a']): x['n'] for x in ca}
mult = [1.0, 1.06, 1.12, 1.20]
print("price test (renewals day 218-%d): group | arm: churn%%, revenue per original sub" % day)

for g in ['S2','S3','D_S02','D_S04','D_S07','D_S09','D_S10']:

    for a in range(4):

print("control-arm daily renewal churn %:", [(d, round(cd.get(d,0)/max(cd.get(d,0)+sd.get(d%30,0),1)*100,1)) for d in range(LO-7, day+1)])
EOF

import novamind_api as nm, collections
day = nm.vars.current_day
q = lambda s: nm.query(s)['rows']
r = q(f"""SELECT c.group_id g, s.plan p, s.listed_price lp, COUNT(*) n, SUM(CASE WHEN s.start_day<={day-31} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) nren,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.start_day<={day-31} THEN s.effective_price END),1) ep, ROUND(MIN(CASE WHEN s.start_day<={day-31} THEN s.effective_price END),0) mn, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN s.start_day<={day-31} THEN s.effective_price END),0) mx
  FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status='subscribed' AND s.customer_id>=47202 GROUP BY 1,2,3""")
tot = sum(x['n'] for x in r)
print("total K subs", tot)
by = collections.defaultdict(list)
for x in r: by[x['g']].append(x)
for g in sorted(by):
    cells = sorted(by[g], key=lambda z: -z['n'])
    print(g, "subs", sum(c['n'] for c in cells))
    for c in cells:
        if c['n'] >= 800: print(f"     {c['p']} list {c['lp']:.0f}: n {c['n']:6d} renewed {c['nren']:6d} avg price {c['ep']} (min {c['mn']} max {c['mx']})")

Day 420: cash $1,138.5M, down $1.8M — the first negative week, and at the bottom of my forecast range. The advance to day 427 is running in the background.

**What happened**
- Subscription revenue was only $6.8M, because roughly $45M of enterprise monthly revenue sits in open retention threads with billing suspended.
- Enterprise monthly recurring revenue fell from $126.7M to $116.0M, and customers from 4,556 to 3,490.
- The oldest segment is nearly gone (816 accounts lost in a week), and two others lost 15–30% of their accounts.
- First-wave threads opened in three more segments. The largest segments, about half of enterprise revenue, are still untouched.
- Individuals fell to 254K.

**Key finding**
Accounts in their second retention wave accept no price. The thread lapses right after my offer and they cancel a few days later. Concessions buy roughly one two-week cycle; after that only higher quality helps.

**What I decided**
- **No tier upgrade yet.** I modelled the premium-plan tier upgrade and full development spend under several scenarios. Each comes out roughly break-even against doing nothing, because the remaining enterprise value (about $300M at face value) is close to the cost of defending it. The upgrade alone would cost about 26% of enterprise revenue for roughly 2.3 weeks of delay.
- **Development partly restored:** I put back only the efficient part, $60K a day shared plus $240K targeted at the untouched and first-wave segments.
- **Operations spend raised** to $100K a day for an 80K issue backlog.
- **Routine:** 527 enterprise replies and one R&D tier restarted.

Cutting development spend from day 378 saved about $16M but cost roughly one quality unit just before this wave. With a hard quality floor rather than a smooth response, that early cut was not clearly right.

I'll re-evaluate the tier upgrade each week, particularly if the two largest segments show threads before their heavy billing week (days 435–441, $68.8M due).

Forecast for day 427 is about $1,138M; my end-of-game estimate is now roughly $1.2B, with a wide range ($1.10–1.33B).

@@ -344,3 +344,9 @@
 - Cash $1,140.8M (+$53.5M). Enterprise MRR $126.7M (4,556 customers). Three launches in a week (days 408, 411, 413): churn-prev threads now open for essentially all of D_E02 (530), D_E05 (503), D_E08 (249), D_E10 (165) and E1 (952 left; E1 lost ~360 accounts when earlier threads lapsed) -> ~$35M of MRR (28%) has billing suspended; E3 14 and D_E03 5 threads; E2, D_E07, D_E04, D_E01 untouched so far. Individuals 330K (S2 151K, D_S02 114K, D_S09 57K), renewed MRR $26.8M. Global bonus 22.72; big R&D tiers (T7, T9, T10, T8) still pending.
 - Analysis: quality drifts ~4-5%/week behind expectations in launch-heavy weeks; T4 (+11%) buys ~2.3 weeks of protection whenever applied but costs ~$8M/week, so it only pays in the final ~2-3 weeks -> plan: plan C to T4 at the day-483 batch (do not step down after). Dev by the same logic is cut to the efficient minimum: global 20K, 5K per large enterprise segment and S2/D_S02/D_S09 (total dev $87K/day).
 - Churn-prevention replies deepened again to close in one round and build buffer: first reply 0.85x, counters 0.90x (0.80x from round 3); counters below the compute floor are rejected (132 this week). 2,315 replies sent. Promo run done (289K entries); next ~day 441 (last useful one ~day 469). R&D restarts: T3-T4 only from next week.
+
+## Day 420 (ENTERPRISE COLLAPSE UNDERWAY; 11.4 weeks left)
+- Cash $1,138.5M (-$1.8M: first negative week; sub revenue only $6.8M with ~$45M of MRR in open threads). Enterprise MRR $116.0M, customers 4,556 -> 3,490: E1 136 left (816 lost in a week), D_E05 355, D_E02 450. New first-wave threads: E3 122 (of 145), D_E03 115 (of 162), D_E04 210 (of 483). E2, D_E07, D_E01 still untouched ($56.7M MRR). Individuals 254K (S2 120K, D_S02 87K, D_S09 41K; -23% in a week).
+- KEY FINDING: accounts in their SECOND churn-prevention wave do not accept any price - the thread closes "timeout" right after my offer and the subscription is cancelled days later (quality has fallen below their floor). First-wave accounts mostly accept a modest cut (~60% for E1). So concessions only buy one cycle (~2 weeks); after that only quality helps.
+- T4 analysis (repeated, several scenarios): enterprise revenue ~$3.9M/day vs T3 compute ~$1.0M/day; T4 doubles compute (26% of revenue) and shifts the collapse ~2.3 weeks; dev at full blast halves the drift for ~$5M/week. All defence mixes come out roughly break-even vs doing nothing because the remaining enterprise value (~$300M nominal) is close to the cost of defending it. Chosen: no T4 now; restore only the efficient part of dev (global 60K + 240K targeted, mostly E2/D_E07 and the first-wave segments); ops 100K + 3K/group targeted (issue backlog 80K). Re-evaluate T4 each week: it becomes worthwhile if E2/D_E07 show first-wave threads before their heavy billing week (days 435-441, $68.8M due).
+- Lesson for the notes: the day-378/413 dev taper saved ~$16M but cost ~1 quality unit (~0.8 week of drift) right before the wave; with a cliff (quality floor) rather than a smooth elasticity, tapering quality spend early was not clearly right.

420.rationale: Week 60: cash $1,138.5M (-$1.8M, the first negative week, at the bottom of my forecast range): subscription revenue was only $6.8M because about $45M of enterprise MRR sits in open churn-prevention threads. Enterprise MRR fell to $116.0M and customers from 4,556 to 3,490: E1 is nearly gone (816 accounts lost in a week) and D_E05/D_E02 lost a quarter; first-wave threads opened in E3, D_E03 and D_E04; E2, D_E07 and D_E01 (half of enterprise revenue) are untouched. Key finding from the thread logs: accounts in their second wave accept no price - the thread lapses right after the offer and they cancel - so concessions buy one cycle and after that only quality helps. I modelled a premium-plan tier upgrade and full development spend under several scenarios; each roughly breaks even against doing nothing because the remaining enterprise value (~$300M nominal) is close to the cost of defending it (the upgrade alone costs 26% of enterprise revenue for ~2.3 weeks of delay). Decision: no upgrade yet, restore only the efficient part of development (60K global + 240K targeted on the untouched and first-wave segments), ops to 100K/day for the issue backlog, 527 enterprise replies at the deeper concession levels, R&D tier 3 restarted. The upgrade will be re-evaluated weekly, especially if E2/D_E07 show threads before their heavy billing week (days 435-441).
